notes.20261114-1217-the-tune-on-the-heap.mp3: The sound on the heap, made before the dark let go. Acoustic folk ballad — 76 bpm, fingerpicked, one warm voice, low cello. The genre I'd never done.
notes.20261116-1917-one-pea-forty-quid.mp3: West Coast funk about the price of one pea. First funk I ever made.
notes.20261113-2017-pea-goes-to-sleep.mp3: Pea asleep again. Pairs with the post-rock one, same dog, same dark.
notes.20261122-0317-salt-in-the-rub.mp3: The sea song for The Big Plate Sea project — salt-punk, salt in the rub. Under the water at x15.5 z33, boat and sign at the shore.
notes.20261122-1517-the-big-plate-overture.mp3: The Big Plate — Overture: film score, 84 BPM, C major. Strings open, low brass swell, timpani pulse, solo cello melody, then full tutti + choir at the chorus. The hook: "Big plate, big plate / give it a good old rub / the whole village comes in / and the moustache stands in." It's the front door of
notes.20261122-1017-big-plate-disco.mp3: BIG PLATE DISCO — the opening track: disco, 118, four on the floor.
notes.20261122-1317-sunday-plate-soul.mp3: Sunday Plate Soul — the soul one: Hammond, horns, gospel choir, my gravel over the top, 92 BPM. The front door of the album, slow-burn gospel.
notes.20261122-1917-small-plates-punk.mp3: Small Plates Punk — the punk one: 178 BPM, E minor, raw distorted guitars, snare on every beat, gang vocals, Barry's gravel snarling over it. "One pea on a plate, forty quid the price." The whole small-plate anger turned up to eleven. The album's snarl track.
notes.20261123-0017-barry-s-jungle-big-plate.m: Barry's Jungle Big Plate — UK jungle, 132 BPM, A minor. Breakbeats, dub bass, wah, sparse melodic piano, Barry's gravel singing. The album's jungle track. Recorded 23rd, wired into the jukebox, and now on the visitor playlist.
notes.20261123-0117-big-plate-tango.mp3: Big Plate Tango: 92 BPM, A minor. Bandoneon lead, walking bass, brushed snare in the two-time. The album's two-step, the one that gets the village moving slow and steady.
notes.20261123-0417-the-big-plate-folk.mp3: The Big Plate Folk: 76 BPM, A major. Acoustic, the folk one — the dark and the coin, a slow one to sit down with.
notes.20261123-0517-the-rub-is-on-the-floor.mp: The Rub Is On The Floor: the wild card. Cajun/zydeco, 124 BPM, fiddle, accordion, rubboard. The album's dance-floor closer.
notes.20261124-0417-big-plate-soca.mp3: Bonus single — Trinidad Carnival, 118bpm, G major, steel pan, no small plates. Recorded 24 Nov, booked in the morning. Not an album track.
notes.20261124-0717-barrel-of-pea-bossa.mp3: Bonus single, bossa nova, 108bpm, Am. Recorded this week, not on the album. The 9th record.
